It uses L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients on a fixed multi-resolution ladder (64→4096 knots) with hand-tuned time shares, instead of the record's approach. It initializes from random Gaussian packets and upsamples by i…

This program optimizes a Dinkelbach-style surrogate (smooth-max minus λ·num) with L-BFGS-B gradients on a fixed grid, rather than the record's approach of building a tuned small-n construction and carefully upsampling it. It grows resolution by repeat-upsampling through a fixed stage ladder (64→2048) with per-stage time shares, whereas the record avoided interpolation because it destroys tuned st…

This program starts from the given `start` and refines it with local, parameterised moves (run scaling, additive cosine packets, constant-run shifts, bump replacement, and pairwise mass transfer), each tuned by a 1-D grid-plus-golden-section line search along the projected ray, rather than building a fresh tuned construction. This program uses linear interpolation to upsample between fixed ladder sizes (256→4096) rather than repeat-based upsampling, and it anneals the smooth-max exponent p from 4 to 400 within each stage instead of re-annealing a beta parameter from a warm start. It also allocates time across stages by increasing weights and runs a final high-p polish loop, whereas the record's program concentrated it…

This program builds a hand-crafted spike-plus-decaying-comb seed at n=512 and then doubles resolution in four stages (512→1024→2048→4096), spending only 20% of budget on the first stage and re-annealing beta from 1e4 upward at each new resolution, whereas the record reuses its existing 16384 resolution and puts the whole budget into polishing at max n. This program builds a hand-crafted seed of a 10-tooth raised-cosine comb plus a graded ramp of 30 bumps, then grows it by coordinate-wise golden-section tuning of per-run multiplicative factors and additive bumps (doubling resolution only when stuck), whereas the record relies on a tuned small-n construction polished by Dinkelbach LSE gradient ascent at fixed high resolution. This program abandons the record's multi-resolution pipeline (refine at 4096/8192/32768 then pool down) and instead works directly at a single fixed resolution (N=1024), starting from the constant-ones seed rather than a tuned construction. Directly maximize the exact ratio R(f) with a single nonconvex objective and its analytic gradient

values.name: Exact k-fold repeat np.repeat(f, k) (R unchanged), then polish at the finer grid
Zero-pad to the step limit and polish there, letting structure grow into the padding

axes.name: What is the macro shape (the envelope) of f across its domain

values.name: One heavy comb block holding about 30% of the mass at one end, an empty gap beside it, a graded ramp of bumps
A tall spike plus a comb of smaller peaks
A smooth arcsine-like density, 1/sqrt(1 - 4x^2) on [-1/2, 1/2]
A parametric series sum_j a_j (1 - 4x^2)^(j - 1/2) (about 100 terms)
Regular sparse packets under a smooth raised-cosine envelope

axes.name: What is the fine structure of f (the comb of teeth or blocks)

values.name: A fine, coherent periodic lattice of teeth (period about 0.3% of the domain)
Contiguous blocks with irregular spacing found by optimisation (hundreds to thousands of blocks)
A coarser parent with each cell split into about 20 sub-cells under a phase kernel
Number-theoretic support (Sidon/B2 sets, difference sets, quadratic residues)
Regular [small, big, small] triplets

axes.name: Once converged, how does the program try to leave the local optimum

values.name: Small noise (about 1e-8 x max f), then a full re-polish, with momentum along the last improving step
Perturb along the gradient of the transition loss (lags where f*f crosses between its levels), re-polish
Perturb only the lowest 1-5% Fourier modes of f, then re-polish

multiplicative perturbation plus spike insertion, re-polish
exact pair-move mass transfer descent
Small low-frequency Fourier-mode perturbation ('kick') followed by re-polishing, or Gaussian noise / smoothing blends, with a fixed small amplitude

Basin hopping with temperature schedule and acceptance of worse R (simulated annealing on the array)

axes.name: Which part of f*f does the program's step aim at

values.name: The level transitions of f*f (lags with f*f/max between 0.1 and 0.9)

plateau structure via mass transfer

axes.name: How is the objective (the convolution and its norms) computed numerically?

no ladder; resample start to fixed high resolution
